size_pct_nav: Incremental-capital stance, not a documented full-market liquidation or exact cash target

drivers.driver: Starting valuations, interest rates and profits constrained aggregate returns far below popular expectations.
Technological transformation did not automatically produce attractive shareholder economics.
High prices and uncertainty about winners supported withholding new equity capital rather than predicting the next market move.
Existing sound franchises were not automatically sold because the aggregate market was expensive.

entry_valuation_stated: Fortune data ~29.6x 1998 reported profits on March 15 market value; article's conditional aggregate-return case ~6% nominal / ~4% real.
outcome_note: HOLD_CASH label means withholding unattractive incremental equity capital, not proof of a large November cash purchase or a Nasdaq short. 1999 letter is post-cutoff corroboration, dated 2000-03-01.
sources: Fortune, November 22, 1999, historical figures and arithmetic only; investor verdict and recommendations withheld; https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/1999ar/FortuneMagazine.pdf ; prior Berkshire annual report; fund reference https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1998htm.html
pack_quality_notes: Market-stance mapping is interpretive: Fortune is a return-expectations essay, not a transaction order.
